terms.meaning: Two or more people communicating through language and symbols and influencing each other.
Showing feelings with gestures and facial expressions, useful when we don't share a language.
Knowing what is expected of each role, and acting to match it.
A fixed belief held without scientific proof, such as thinking women know less than men.

items.name: Why general knowledge isn't enough
items.example: Sociology can show by study that women are as capable as men.

items.name: What sociology helps us do
items.example: It gives correct information for daily life.

items.name: Language and where we live
items.formula: We learn the language that suits our surroundings.
items.example: Without a shared language, daily life is hard.

items.name: Example of role consciousness
items.formula: The doctor prescribes and the nurse cares for the patient as told.
items.example: You don't ask the teacher for medicine or the doctor about lessons.

items.name: Many roles of one person
items.formula: In a family one can be brother, son and grandson at once.
items.example: Roles change with age and conditions.

mistakes.text: Social interaction needs more than one person; it is between people, not inside one person.
A common saying is not a scientific truth. Sociology checks claims by study.
A person doesn't have just one role: everyone plays several at once.
